Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Persian هندو (hendu).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈhindu/, [ˈhindu]
  • Rhymes: -indu
  • Syllabification(key): hin‧du
  • Hyphenation(key): hin‧du

Noun

[edit]

hindu

  1. Hindu (person)

Hungarian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Persian هندو (hendu, “Indian, Hindu”), from Middle Persian hndwk' (Hindūg, “Indian”), from hnd (Hind, “India”) + -wk' (-ūg), from Old Persian 𐏃𐎡𐎯𐎢 (hindu-, “India”), from Sanskrit सिन्धु (síndhu, “river, stream; Indus”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *síndʰuš (“river”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈhindu]
  • Hyphenation: hin‧du
  • Rhymes: -du

Adjective

[edit]

hindu (comparative hindubb, superlative leghindubb)

  1. Hindu (of or relating to Hinduism)

Livvi

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Finnic *hinta, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic *śímta.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈhʲindu/
  • Hyphenation: hin‧du
  • Rhymes: -indu

Noun

[edit]

hindu

  1. price

Norwegian Bokmål

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Persian هندو (hendu, “Indian, Hindu”), from Middle Persian hndwk' (Hindūg, “Indian”), from hnd (Hind, “India”) + -wk' (-ūg), from Old Persian 𐏃𐎡𐎯𐎢 (hindu-, “India”), from Sanskrit सिन्धु (síndhu, “river, stream; Indus”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *sindʰus (“river”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /hɪndʉ/
  • Rhymes: -ɪndʉ

Noun

[edit]

hindu m (definite singular hinduen, indefinite plural hinduer, definite plural hinduene)

  1. a Hindu

Derived terms

[edit]
  • hinduisk
  • hinduisme
  • hinduistisk

References

[edit]
  • “hindu” in The Bokmål Dictionary.

Norwegian Nynorsk

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Persian هندو (hendu, “Indian, Hindu”), from Middle Persian hndwk' (Hindūg, “Indian”), from hnd (Hind, “India”) + -wk' (-ūg), from Old Persian 𐏃𐎡𐎯𐎢 (hindu-, “India”), from Sanskrit सिन्धु (síndhu, “river, stream; Indus”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *sindʰus (“river”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /hɪndʉ/
  • Rhymes: -ɪndʉ

Noun

[edit]

hindu m (definite singular hinduen, indefinite plural hinduar, definite plural hinduane)

  1. a Hindu

Derived terms

[edit]
  • hinduisk
  • hinduisme

References

[edit]
  • “hindu” in The Nynorsk Dictionary.

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Persian هندو (hendu, “Indian, Hindu”), from Middle Persian hndwk' (Hindūg, “Indian”), from hnd (Hind, “India”), from Old Persian 𐏃𐎡𐎯𐎢 (hindu-, “India”), from Sanskrit सिन्धु (síndhu, “river, stream; Indus”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *sindʰus (“river”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ĩˈdu/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ĩˈdu/

  • Rhymes: -u
  • Hyphenation: hin‧du

Adjective

[edit]

hindu m or f (plural hindus)

  1. Hindu

Further reading

[edit]
  • “hindu”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “hindu”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026
